title: Google further buries search results under AI mode
content:
Google is now automatically expanding its AI search summaries at the top of the results page for some searches, as reported by Search Engine Roundtable. The change, when it kicks in, pushes the typical list of links from a search much farther down Google’s results page; instead of seeing part of an AI Overview with a “Show more” button you can click, you’ll Google will show a full AI Overview at the top of your search, an “Ask anything” box under that, and then the list of links. It can lead to a lot of scrolling.
Google further buries search results under AI mode
Google now automatically expands its AI search summaries for some queries.
It’s unclear exactly what Google’s criteria is for the auto-expanding AI Overviews. Before writing this story, I was seeing them with most of my test searches. But now, AI Overviews usually just show the initial part of the response and the “Show more” button. My most consistent query to get the auto-expanding AI Overview is “what is the best game on switch 2”, but even that hasn’t been consistent across searches and browsers.
“For some queries, AI Overviews may dynamically expand for topics where our systems determine it’s most useful for people,” Google spokesperson Jennifer Kutz says in a statement to The Verge. “Our research has shown that with this dynamic experience, users find Search more helpful and engage deeper in follow-up exploration.” Kutz also says that “If users have already begun scrolling to view content below the AI Overview, we cancel expansion so that the user doesn’t lose their reading position.”

report.summary: Google now auto-expands AI Overviews for some queries, pushing web links further down results and deepening AI-first search.
report.background: Google introduced AI Overviews last year as part of its broader push to embed generative AI into Search. The feature initially stumbled with visible accuracy issues, but Google has steadily refined it and expanded its presence. This latest change removes the manual 'Show more' step for certain queries, instead displaying a fully expanded AI answer, an 'Ask anything' follow-up box, and then the traditional link list. Google says the expansion is dynamic and based on whether the system determines it will be most useful, though the exact criteria remain opaque. The move fits a clear strategic pattern: as AI models like Gemini improve, Google increasingly prioritizes conversational answers over blue links, reshaping how users interact with search results and potentially reducing traffic to external websites.
key_points: For a subset of searches, Google now shows complete AI Overviews automatically at the top of the results page, eliminating the 'Show more' click and pushing organic links much lower. Google says this happens only when its systems judge that expanded answers are useful for the query.

The behavior is inconsistent across queries and browsers. One reporter consistently triggered the expanded view with 'what is the best game on switch 2', but even that query failed to expand reliably, suggesting the triggering rules depend on many unpredictable factors.

Google claims that if a user begins scrolling to the results below, the expansion is canceled so the reader doesn't lose their position. This indicates the company is trying to balance AI-first answers with user control, though it still means less visible web links for many searches.

For publishers and SEO specialists, this change accelerates the decline of traditional organic visibility. Even if a site ranks first in links, the AI Overview can consume most of the screen and answer the query without click-through, making it harder to measure and earn referral traffic.

Google frames the expanded AI mode as a tool for deeper follow-up exploration, citing internal research that says users find Search more helpful. This points to a long-term vision where Search becomes a conversational layer rather than a list of sources.
report.impact: This change signals that Google is fully committed to an AI-first search experience, which will likely pressure competitors like Bing to accelerate their own AI rollouts. For developers and SEO professionals, the practical takeaway is that visibility now depends on being quoted inside AI Overviews, not just ranking in traditional links. That shifts optimization toward structured data, clear factual answers, and content designed for LLM extraction. Regular users may enjoy quicker answers to simple questions, but they lose straightforward access to the web results behind those answers. The 'Ask anything' box also nudges users into an extended conversation with Gemini, keeping them inside Google's ecosystem rather than sending them elsewhere. While Google says the expansion respects scrolling behavior, the net effect is less real estate for independent content and a search page that increasingly mirrors a chatbot interface.
report.tools: To monitor how AI Overviews affect your site, Google Search Console provides impressions and clicks for AI-related results. For building your own AI search experiments, the Gemini API offers direct model access, and open-source frameworks like LangChain or LlamaIndex can help construct retrieval pipelines. SEO platforms like Ahrefs and Semrush are adding AI visibility tracking features. If you're curious about how these summaries get generated, Google's official AI Overview documentation explains current policies and best practices for appearing in them.
